title: Spec: Lexicon v0 (M0 to M5)

comments.body:
## Spec, part 2: supersessions and moved tickets

GitHub's issue size limit splits the spec here. This comment belongs to the spec's Further Notes.

### Supersessions (later ticket beats the grill record or earlier research)

1. **Cloud speech:** the grill's default (MAI-Transcribe-2 via OpenRouter) is replaced by Meta Muse streamed over its own WebSocket. OpenRouter is out of the speech path (no streaming). (Fastest path from speech to text; Best streaming speech provider; Speech pipeline.)
2. **Speech in M0:** the map's "M0 cloud model" and the architecture's "M0 Muse adapter" are replaced by local Parakeet only for M0 and M1; Muse lands in M2. M2's name changes from "Works offline" to "Cloud and Private mode", since offline works from M0. (Speech pipeline.)
3. **Race cutoff:** 0.8 s after fn-up (speech research, architecture) is replaced by 300 ms after recording stops. (Speech pipeline.)
4. **Capture tail:** a fixed 200 ms is replaced by an adaptive tail, stop on silence, max 200 ms. (Speech pipeline.)
5. **Jev:** via Vercel AI Gateway (`typesafe-ai/jev`, which can't pin a version) is replaced by TypeSafe direct with `jev-1.13.0` pinned. (Jev from Swift; Confirm Jev access.)
6. **Jev for close calls** (grill D4, vocab research, Private mode ticket, architecture M4) is dropped; Jev is for Re-speak and Hand fixes only. (The Lexicon.)
7. **Terms to speech:** 50 to 100, or about 100 to Meta, is replaced by up to 50. (The Lexicon.)
8. **Local word boosting:** FluidAudio boosting in Private mode is dropped; Rules in code instead. (Best local speech model; The Lexicon.)
9. **Cleanup:** the research's "no LLM by default" is replaced by AI cleanup on by default; the 250 ms p95 budget is replaced by a deadline that keeps total lag within the pass mark (about 450 ms; the amendment said at or under Wispr's 740 ms p50, the later lag target is 700 ms); Apple Foundation Models is out for now, so Private mode and offline use rules only. (Cleanup pass and its amendment; LLM cleanup research.)
10. **Every Fix becomes a Rule** (grill D6) is replaced by: every Re-speak fix becomes a Test set entry immediately (Hand fixes follow in M5); when a Fix becomes a Rule is the after-M1 grill.
11. **Head-to-head:** BlackHole virtual mic and synthetic fn (grill D7, harness research) are dropped; Wispr is scored from its own logs. (The Test set and 'beats Wispr'.)
12. **Wispr's lag:** "about 0.6 s" from a competitor benchmark is replaced by Wispr's own logs on Jake's Mac: p50 740 ms, p95 1,671 ms. (Fastest path from speech to text; Build the Test set.)
13. **Toolchain:** Xcode 26.6 plus XcodeGen and an Apple Development identity (build research) are replaced by Command Line Tools only and the self-signed "Lexicon Dev" certificate. (ADR 0003; Install Command Line Tools.)
14. **fn:** the system double-click interval (0.5 s) is replaced by 0.25 s; Fn+Space and the fallback hotkey are dropped from v0. (fn and recording behavior.)
15. **Sounds:** "start and stop chimes" are now soft synthesized blips, pitched lower. (Recording indicator.)
16. **Glossary:** Rule now means "added by the user or learned from a confirmed Fix"; Lexicon now means "Terms and Rules"; Term was added. Follow-up for the M0 doc update: the Secret guard entry says it keeps a Dictation from leaving the Mac, but audio already streamed can't be recalled (Private mode amendment 2); reword it to "keeps keys, tokens and passwords out of every text call and cuts the speech stream".
17. **Code context (grill D5):** "package names, function names, file names" is narrowed to names only: repo names, dependency names, skill and slash-command names, bold glossary terms; no identifiers or file names. (The Lexicon.)
18. **Active-app formatting (grill D5):** no per-app styles in v0; light app-specific formatting moves to the after-M1 grill. (Cleanup pass.)
19. **Meaning check:** the research's `verify()` ("output equals raw text minus listed fillers") is replaced by the structural check, which allows AI 

(cut for the fixture)

## Later (Reviewer)

Non-blocking notes from PR reviews. One list, edited in place. Jake promotes an item to an issue when he wants it.

### From #92 (skeleton, merged as e2c850b): sketch code that disagrees with the spec

The sketch came over as it was; #38 changed only the shared defaults. These comments and stub values contradict the spec and will mislead whoever fills the bodies. Fix them in the ticket that fills each body, or in one small cleanup ticket.

- `Sources/Transcription/RacePolicy.swift:24` says "after the deadline, the first finished engine wins". Spec: the cloud wins only within 300 ms after recording stops, otherwise local wins. (race ticket, M2)
- `Sources/Transcription/RacePolicy.swift:9` `cloudRetries = 1`. Spec: a cloud error goes straight to local. (M2)
- `Sources/Cleanup/StructuralCheck.swift:25` `lengthCap = 1.3`. Spec: about 1.2. (#74)
- `Sources/Cleanup/Cleanup.swift:10,64,77,108`, `CleanupModel.swift:54`, `LexiconDomain/CleanupResult.swift:23`, `scripts/check-imports.swift` (FoundationModels allowed in Cleanup): Apple Foundation Models as the Private mode and offline cleanup. Spec: out for now; Private mode and offline are rules only. (#42, #75)
- `Sources/Cleanup/Cleanup.swift:77` builds a cloud cleanup engine whenever AI cleanup is on and access exists. "Inert until M3" isn't enforced, so an OpenRouter key in M2 would send text before the structural check exists. (#42, #75)
- `Sources/Cleanup/TextPass.swift:10,28` keeps the research `verify` step and active-app formatting (supersessions 18, 19). (#42)
- Jev close calls are still seamed in: `Jev/JevClient.swift:45`, `Fixes/FixEngine.swift:38,50`, `WordStore/Lexicon.swift:25`, `LexiconDomain/Fix.swift:13,22` (`FixKind.auto`, `FixSource.closeCall`). Supersession 6 drops them.
- `KeyInput/EventTap.swift:12` accepts synthetic fn "for the head-to-head harness" (supersession 11 drops it). Any local process could start a recording. (#53)
- `KeyInput/Keyboard.swift:31` `fallbackHotkey` seam; out of scope for v0. `FnGesture` has no other-key-cancel note for fn+Shift (open question 3), needed before M4.
- `AppText/InsertGuard.swift:33` has no input for the spec's "same app and under 5 s" fallback when a field can't be detected. The signature needs a time input. (#60)
- `LexiconDomain/Words.swift:14` says Rules come only from confirmed Fixes, and `Rule` has no added/learned source field; `WordStore/Lexicon.swift:65` lists a `contacts` source the spec lacks.
- 586 MB in `AppPaths.swift:14` and `ParakeetTranscriber.swift:10,29`; spec says about 609 MB.
- Stale: `Cleanup/CleanupModel.swift:9` (15.5 SDK), `LexiconUI/AppUI.swift:8` (design.md doesn't exist), `AudioCapture/Recorder.swift:71` (sleep listed as an immediate stop; spec says normal stop), `Preferences.swift:27` ("fixed in code" on a persisted field).

### From #92: sketch logic to fix when the bodies are filled

- `LexiconCore/Conductor+Run.swift:107-119`: the waiting branch never calls `releaseInsertTurn`, so one outage blocks every later insert (contradicts `Conductor.swift:50`). It also retries with the fn-down `CloudAccess`, so Private mode turned on mid-wait can still send audio, and it has no backoff when `networkReturned()` returns at once. (#59)
- `History/Schema.swift:101-115` `RecoveryPlan`: a row left in `ready` is non-terminal, so the TODO sends it to `.transcribe` and it lands `.recovered`, not `.notInserted(.interrupted)` as `HistoryStore.recover` promises. Needs its own action. (#59)
- `LexiconCore/Conductor+Run.swift:157`: `fixes.respeak` runs for any `.respeak` purpose, including a recovered one, and `TargetApp.replace` takes no `Target`. Recovered Re-speak text could edit another app. Gate on a live target. (M4)
- `LexiconCore/Conductor.swift:102` `justFixed` grants `CloudAccess` with `app: .unknown`, skipping the always-private check. Use the focused app. (M5)

body:
Spec for **Lexicon v0** (milestones M0 to M5), collapsed from the map [Wayfinder: Lexicon v0](https://github.com/jparker2006/lexicon/issues/1). Each decision lives in its map ticket; this spec gathers them into one buildable plan. Where the original grill record and a later ticket disagree, the ticket wins (see "Supersessions" under Further Notes). Words follow GLOSSARY.md.

> **Open questions for Jake** at the end of Further Notes are all decided (2026-10-11).

## Problem Statement

Jake dictates prompts to coding agents all day, mostly into the Claude desktop app (Code tab) and Codex inside the ChatGPT desktop app, but everywhere on his Mac. He uses Wispr Flow and pays for it. It gets tech words wrong in ways he can't blame on himself ("super base", "work tree", "codecs"), it barely learns, correcting text afterwards is painful, it doesn't work off wifi, he can't pick the speech model, and the app is big and slow. Wispr's own logs on his Mac show its lag: half of Dictations within 740 ms, 95% within 1,671 ms.

The bottom line: if a replacement is worse than Wispr Flow on Jake's own voice, he won't use it. It has to get fewer words wrong, fewer tech words wrong, be at least as fast, work offline, and never lose a Dictation.

## Solution

Lexicon: a native Swift menu bar app, AppKit only, that is ridiculously fast and ridiculously small.

- **Same feel as Wispr.** Hold fn to talk, release to insert. Double-tap fn for hands-free, tap fn to stop. Text lands at the cursor in any app.
- **Never loses a Dictation.** Audio is on disk within the first 100 ms. Every Dictation is saved in History. Text that arrives late, or has nowhere to go, waits for paste-last instead of being typed into the wrong place.
- **Fast speech, online or off.** Lexicon streams audio to the best cloud model while Jake talks (Meta Muse by default, switchable) and races a local model (Parakeet Unified) on every Dictation. Whichever is ready in time wins. Offline and Private mode use the local model only.
- **Wispr-quality Cleanup.** Rules in code, then an AI cleanup model with a hard deadline and a structural check, falling back to rules-only text so nothing waits or changes meaning.
- **Learns Jake's words.** A Lexicon of Terms and Rules, seeded from his Wispr history and his code, fixes spelling-form misses instantly in code and steers both models.
- **Fix by voice.** Hold fn+Shift and say the right word, and Lexicon replaces the misheard word in what he just dictated.
- **Proven, not claimed.** A private Test set built from Jake's real Wispr recordings scores every change against Wispr's own logged output. v0 is done when Lexicon passes the "beats Wispr" mark on held-back clips and Jake switches Wispr off (first possible at M3).

What Jake can do after each milestone:

| Milestone | Jake can |
|---|---|
| M0 It types | Hold fn, talk, and see text at the cursor, using the local model. Menu bar icon, recording pill, sounds. |
| M1 Never loses it | Dictate hands-free, open History, copy any Dictation, paste the last one with ⌃⌘V, and lose no Dictation on a crash (at most about 0.1 s of audio). |
| M2 Cloud and Private mode | Get cloud speech racing the local model, switch to Private mode, add keys and pick models in Settings. |
| M3 Good enough to swap | Get Wispr-level Cleanup and his Lexicon, see Lexicon beat Wispr on the Test set, and turn Wispr off. |
| M4 Fix by voice | Fix a misheard word by holding fn+Shift and saying it. |
| M5 Learns from you | Hand fixes, learned Rules and light app formatting, designed in an "after M1" grill. |

## User Stories

### Dictating

1. As Jake, I want to hold fn and talk, so that text appears at my cursor when I let go.
2. As Jake, I want recording to start the instant fn goes down, so that my first word is never clipped.
3. As Jake, I want a hold of 0.30 s or more to count as push-to-talk, so that quick taps don't start Dictations by accident.

title: M0: Never-lose audio file writer
body:
## Parent

#36 (Spec: Lexicon v0)

**Milestone:** M0  
**User stories:** 22  
**Test seam:** headless (file input)  
**Modules:** AudioCapture

## What to build

The writer every Dictation's audio goes through, proven with file input before any mic exists. Audio is written to `audio/<id>.caf` as 16 kHz mono 16-bit PCM, packets about every 100 ms, `F_FULLFSYNC` every 1 s and at stop, off any real-time thread. Resampling uses the converter (minimum phase, max quality). Banned: async file writes, direct FLAC, WAV via AudioFile. A capture can be stopped at most once (non-copyable type with a consuming stop).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A synthetic 16 kHz WAV fed through the writer reads back bit-exact.
- [ ] Killing the writer process mid-write leaves a CAF that reads back bit-exact up to the last flush (data size left unset).
- [ ] Stopping twice is a compile error.

## Blocked by

- #38
